full_narration: Can a simple timer turn scattered work into focus? She reaches for the book, opening it. Inside, pages reveal Francesco Cirillo creating the Pomodoro Technique. He used a tomato timer while studying. The method divides work into twenty five minute sessions. Short breaks reset attention before another session begins. The idea spread from one student's habit to a global practice. Workers ignore distractions as their goals become clearer. The technique works because focus gets a protected space.
